description.narrative: The project is implemented in South Africa. The main outcome areas it contributes to are democracy and human rights. The main rights holders are asylum seekers, refugees and migrants in South Africa and SADC Region. Through advocacy and policy lobbying, trainings, network coordination, educational material development and sharing the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is implemented with the support of The Union for Professionals, Akademikerförbundet SSR.The Consortium for Refugees and Migrants in South Africa (CoRMSA) is an NGO with the aim to promote and protect the rights of refugees, asylum seekers and migrants. CoRMSA has 25 member organisations, ranging from research institutes, national migrant organisations to Lawyers for Human Rights and Amnesty International.Akademikerförbundet SSR is the Swedish association for university graduates in public administration, social science, political science, behavioral science, human resource management or social work. The union organises 70,000 members in both the public and private sectors.Other Donors to the OrganisationKindernotHilfe - donor fundsOpen Society Foundation of South Africa - donor funds.Project ObjectiveTo enhance the social and policy inclusion, protection and integration of non-nationals in South African society and the region.Actor groupsRights holders:Asylum seekers, RefugeesMigrants in South Africa and SADC RegionActor working in cooperation:Local (host) communitiesThe United Nations OrganisationsInternational Organisations working on human rights, democracy and migrationChapter 9 institutionsCivil Society OrganisationsLabour OrganisationsDecision Makers:GovernmentSADC SecretariatAfrican Union BodiesPolitical officials
